summary: L. Johannes Frohnmeyer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Basel Mission (~1871–1876), where he served as inspector of missions from 1876 to 1905, and later became a Fellow of the University of Madras.

L. P. N. Perera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a former supervisor at Vidyodaya Campus, University of Sri Lanka, and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University and studied in Paris. He was Professor of Central Asian Languages at Eötvös Loránd University (1940–1974).

Lajos Lóczy was a scholar of history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Zurich and ETH Zurich (1869–1874), joined the Hungarian National Museum in 1874, and became Professor of Geography at Eötvös Loránd University in 1889.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshman Sarup was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as University Professor of Sanskrit at Panjab University (attested 1947).
Lakshmanacharya worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala, Mathura, attested in 1889 and in 1900 as an अध्यापक.

Lakshmi Swaminathan worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938), and later became a retired lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. under Govind Chandra Pande at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, where he taught before holding posts at Punjabi University and other institutions.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar who served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).
Lama Jabb works in Tibetology. He held a post as Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and is Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester, studied under traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and joined the faculty of the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, served as its Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who received traditional training under numerous teachers, including the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Isebaert is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Albert Joris van Windekens (~1977–1981) and served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1986–2020).

Lambert Schmithausen is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker, taught at the University of Münster (1970–1973), and served on the Advisory Board at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lan Wu is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University (2008–2016), taught at the University of New Mexico (2015–2016), and became an associate professor at Mount Holyoke College in 2023.

Lance E. Nelson works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at McMaster University (completed by 1986) and held a professorship at the University of San Diego (attested 1997; Professor Emeritus 2021).

Lance S. Cousins was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman, lectured at the University of Manchester (~1970–2000), and taught at Oxford (~2000–2015).
